hypotheses.reasoning: auth-svc was healthy until instance auth-svc-3 restarted at 12:06:48 (capacity 3/4). That loss alone is survivable. account-svc then retried POST /tokens immediately with no backoff, up to 4 attempts. Load on auth-svc rose to 3-5x baseline, so it shed load with 503s and the overload persisted. account-svc ran out of retries, so edge-proxy returned 503 on /login. The S3 503s in catalog-svc, the legacy-inventory health check timeouts and the slow audit_log query are unrelated red herrings.
auth-svc may simply have lacked capacity after the restart. The logs show the amplification by retries, not a resource that was too small on its own.

verdict.recommendedAction: Add exponential backoff with jitter and a retry budget to account-svc's AuthClient. Restore auth-svc capacity and check why auth-svc-3 failed its liveness probe. Temporarily throttle /login at the edge so auth-svc can recover.
